Adele: Quick FYI — ran a mixed-model perf sweep this morning (Llama2-70B, Mixtral-8x, Qwen-7B). Saw a regression when enabling FP8 KV cache + our new adaptive-batching window. p95 jumped on long prefixes.

Mike: Can you paste the numbers?

Adele: Ran identical workload (prefix 8k tokens -> 12k tokens). Baseline (FP16 KV + fixed-batch): p50 18ms p95 120ms. FP8 KV + adaptive window: p50 22ms p95 210ms. Throughput down ~15%.

Sangita: Oof. Any kernel fallbacks in the traces? Those p95s smell like a memcpy/eviction storm.

Adele: Yep — trace shows frequent fallback to generic GEMM at sequence lengths > 4k for Mixtral kernels. Also eviction spikes when adaptive window grows past 1024 tokens.

perf-bot: profile snapshot attached: evictions/sec: 380 -> 2.1k, kv-cache-mem: 11.2GB -> 8.0GB (FP8 stores more compress artifacts), kernel-fallbacks: 6 -> 42.

Igor: Interesting that kv-cache-mem decreased but perf got worse. Suggests extra CPU overhead due to aggressive quant/dequant and eviction thrashing. Did you check prefix-cache hit ratio?

Adele: Hit ratio dropped from 96% -> 78% once adaptive window allowed cross-request consolidation. Looks like prefix alignment changed so cached segments didn’t match new block boundaries after quantization padding.

Mike: Could be RoPE scaling interaction — Llama/Llama-like RoPE implementations can be sensitive to small misalignments when reusing KV blocks, especially with per-head quant offsets. Which models show it most?

Adele: Mixtral worst, then Llama2, Qwen barely affected. Mixtral uses 64-heads/128-kv-dim slices which amplify rounding noise after FP8 pack/unpack.

Sangita: Two hypotheses: (1) FP8 quantization algorithm (per-tensor vs per-channel) introduces tiny value drift so the equality-based cache lookup misses, (2) adaptive-window boundary calc doesn't respect original attention block alignment.

Igor: Reproduce test: run Mixtral with FP8 KV but force block-aligned caching and disable adaptive window. If perf returns -> boundary bug. If not -> quantization issue.

Adele: I ran that: FP8 + block-aligned + fixed-batch = p95 128ms (better, but still ~8% regression vs FP16 baseline). Block misalignment alone explains the big regression.

Mike: Good. Next step: revert adaptive window changes for Mixtral by default, and add a sanitizer that asserts cached-key hashes are within tolerance for quantized formats. Also file a kernel bug: fallback triggers at seq>4k for Mixtral FP8 kernels.

Sangita: I'll open two PRs: one to gate adaptive-window by model config (disable for head-count >= 64 / kv-dim >= 128), and one adding per-channel quant check + soft-compare for cache equality.

Igor: Add a microbenchmark script to eng-runtime perf harness. Sample command:

./perf_runner --model mixtral-8x --kv-format fp8 --cache-policy block-aligned --batching adaptive:disabled --seq-max 12288 --workload conv-prefix

Adele: I'll land a revert flag and collect more traces. For next sync: bring kernel dumps and a small repro script that toggles per-tensor vs per-channel FP8.

perf-bot: task created: PERF-4217 (investigate FP8 KV eviction + RoPE alignment). Assigned: Sangita, Igor. ETA: 2d. :mag:
